Answer the questions on the basis of the information given below.

Information on the number of students studying in 1st to 7th class at Himalaya Primary School in the years 2017 and 2018 is given in the table below. Students enter the school only in 1st class and leave only after passing the 7th class. No new student can enter or leave in any other class.

Students who clear the examination for any class advance to next higher class in the next year. Students who fail to clear the examination for any class continue in the same class in the next year. Also, the number of students failing in any class is a distinct single digit natural number.
questions.question_text: In the year 2017, how many classes had pass percentage greater than overall pass percentage of the school?
questions.solution_text:
Nice puzzle — I solved it. Here's a clean walk-through and the unique solution.
 Setup:
 Let $f_1,...,f_7$ be the number of students who failed in classes 1–7 in 2017 (each is a distinct single-digit natural number).
 Let $N$ be the number of new entrants into 1st class for 2018.
 Rules $ightarrow$ relations:
 Students who pass class $i$ in 2017 (that's $40-f_1$ for class 1, $48-f_2$ for class 2, etc.) move to class $i+1$ in 2018.
 Students who fail stay in the same class next year.
 New students only enter 1st class.
 So the equations for 2018 counts (using the table values) are:
 $N + f_1 = 50$
 $(40 - f_1) + f_2 = 41$
 $(48 - f_2) + f_3 = 46$
 $(53 - f_3) + f_4 = 58$
 $(70 - f_4) + f_5 = 64$
 $(32 - f_5) + f_6 = 36$
 $(44 - f_6) + f_7 = 48$
 Each $f_i$ is in ${1,2,...,9}$ and all are distinct.
 Solution (by solving the system / checking integer possibilities):
 The unique solution that satisfies all equations and the distinct single-digit condition is:
 $f_1 = 3$
 $f_2 = 4$
